summary: We deployed a website powered by a Generalized Additive Model (GAM) that uses the last five years of environmental and satellite data (2021–2025) to predict crop performance across the contiguous United States. Operating on a standardized 55 x 55 km  grid indexed by state, latitude, longitude, and elevation, the platform integrates official records from NASA POWER, MODIS Terra, USDA SSURGO, USDA Cropland Data Layer, and Copernicus DEM.Unlike rigid linear equations, the GAM fits smooth, non-linear curves to capture real-world biological thresholds, such as how temperature extremes, rainfall, and soil water-holding capacity interact to drive plant growth. When a user selects a specific location, the model forecasts expected crop vigor (NDVI) and canopy moisture status (NDMI).These predictions feed into an agronomic scoring engine that rates regional water suitability and calculates soil erosion vulnerability using the USDA Universal Soil Loss Equation framework. Finally, the system combines these risk scores with local baseline crops to recommend tailored, conservation-based crop rotations that protect yields and long-term soil health.
details:
Our project is a predictive agricultural tool designed to optimize crop selection and rotation. It works by dividing target land into a latitude-and-longitude grid and calculating local site parameters, such as soil type, elevation, slope etc, for each square. By matching each squares local parameters to the crop that was planted there, it then uses historical planting datasets with satellite vegetation (NDVI) and moisture (NDMI) indices to train custom Generalized Additive Models (GAMs) for each crop. Once trained, each square’s static geographic traits are locked in, leaving temperature and precipitation as the two dynamic variables.

To make complex climate modeling fast and accessible, our team creatively pre-computes and stores all regressions in a database built with r, JSON and vercel. This eliminates the need to re-run heavy calculations on every use. Depending on the month, weather conditions, and user priorities, the model identifies the best-suited crop for a given square and recommends sustainable follow-up rotation strategies.

By factoring in microclimate variations, computational speed, and farmer priorities, this tool delivers instant, localized planting recommendations. Ultimately, it aims to boost agricultural yields, improve soil health, and help farmers adapt efficiently to changing weather patterns.
